en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Sixth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether the Earth Element is Visible, etc.
Is the earth element visible? Yes.
"Is form, the form-base, the form-element—blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by the eye, impinging upon the eye, and coming into the range of the eye—not to be so stated?
... [as before] ...
"Is the earth-element with visible appearance?"
“Yes,” you say.
“Is it then the case that eye-consciousness arises in dependence upon both the eye and the earth-element?
You must not say so… [and so on].
“Dependent on the eye and the earth element, visual consciousness arises”?
— Yes.
“Dependent on the eye and the earth element, visual consciousness arises”—[is this your position]? — Yes.
Is this indeed a sutta? No.
[It is not.
“Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises”—this is not a sutta.
Is that indeed a sutta? Yes. If so, [does it not say]:
“Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises”?
That sutta passage indeed exists, yet, alas, it should not be said:
“Dependent on the eye and the earth element, eye-consciousness arises.
It should not be so stated.
“Is the earth element visible?”—
Yes. But does one not see the ground, stones, and mountains?
“Yes.
“If one sees earth, stones, and mountains, then indeed, sir, you must say:
‘The earth element is visible’” … and so on … up to … “… it follows that the earth element is not invisible.”
Is it not to be said that the water element is visible?
Yes, it is.
"Does he not see water?
"Yes.
"If he sees water, then indeed, sir, it must be said:"
“Is the water element visible?
… [as before] … “Should it not be said that the fire element is visible?”
“Yes,” he said. “But do you not see the fire burning?
“Yes,” he said.
If one sees a burning fire, then indeed, O friend, it should be said:
“The fire element is visible. … [as before] … It should not be so stated.
“Is the air element visible?”—
“Yes.”—
“But does one not see trees being moved by the wind?”
“Yes, [it is so].
“If one sees a tree being moved by the wind, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
‘The air element is visible’ … [and so on] …”
The discussion on whether the earth element is visible and so forth is finished.
